MEM51.TXT:
+------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                   02 / Memory, addressing and flags                    |
+------------------------------------------------------------------------+

THREE SPACES, ONE NUMBER
CODE is up to 64 KiB of program memory, fetched by PC and read as data
with MOVC. XDATA is a separate, up-to-64-KiB external data space accessed
with MOVX. Internal DATA contains the CPU's small RAM and its directly
addressed special function registers. Thus MOV A,0x30, MOVC A,@A+DPTR and
MOVX A,@DPTR can read three different physical places even if the
numerical address is the same.

INTERNAL MAP (128-byte 80C31)
00-07  register bank 0 (reset default)
08-0F  register bank 1
10-17  register bank 2
18-1F  register bank 3
20-2F  16 bytes / 128 individually addressable RAM bits
30-7F  general RAM and stack, allocated by your program
80-FF  directly addressed SFRs, NOT another 128 RAM bytes

PSW.RS1:RS0 selects the register bank. R3 means the third numbered
register in the CURRENT bank, not invariably address 03. Internal indirect
MOV A,@R0 and MOV @R1,A use RAM only; on an 80C31 there is no upper 80-FF
internal RAM. Never use an indirect pointer above 7F as an SFR shortcut.
An 80C32's extra RAM is a different device feature.

Addressing examples:
    mov a,#0x30      ; A = literal 48
    mov a,0x30       ; A = RAM byte at 30
    mov r0,#0x30
    mov a,@r0        ; same RAM byte, indirect
    mov dptr,#0x1234
    movx a,@dptr     ; external DATA byte at 1234
    clr a
    movc a,@a+dptr   ; CODE byte at 1234

MOVX through @R0/@R1 uses an 8-bit low address; classic external hardware
uses P2's latch for the high address. MOVX @DPTR uses all 16 address bits.
Neither is the same as ordinary MOV @Ri. MOVC uses A as an unsigned index;
the @A+PC base is PC AFTER the MOVC opcode. JMP @A+DPTR also uses an
unsigned byte offset, not a table of pointers automatically dereferenced
by hardware.

BIT MEMORY
Bit addresses 00-7F map to bytes 20-2F: byte = 20 + (bit_address / 8), bit
= bit_address modulo 8. Bit 00 is RAM 20.0; bit 7F is RAM 2F.7. Bit
addresses 80-FF select implemented bit-addressable SFRs whose BYTE address
is divisible by eight. Not every SFR supports bit operations: TMOD at 89
does not. Bit address 89 is TCON.1, not TMOD. Use ANL/ORL on a whole byte
for non-bit-addressable registers.

FLAGS: PSW = CY AC F0 RS1 RS0 OV user P
CY is carry for addition and borrow for SUBB. AC is carry/borrow across
bit 3. OV signals signed arithmetic overflow. P is maintained from A: 1
for an odd number of set bits. F0 is a software flag. The classic CPU has
NO zero or negative flag; JZ/JNZ inspect A itself. INC and DEC do not
update CY or OV. They still affect P if they change A.

For unsigned comparison, CJNE sets CY when its first unsigned operand is
less than the second. For signed comparison you must account for
sign/overflow yourself. Example: 0x7F + 1 becomes 0x80 with OV=1 but CY=0.
Conversely 0xFF + 1 becomes 0 with CY=1 but OV=0.

16-BIT ADD / SUBTRACT
    mov a,0x30       ; low byte of left operand
    add a,0x32       ; low byte of right operand
    mov 0x34,a
    mov a,0x31
    addc a,0x33
    mov 0x35,a       ; final CY is the 16-bit carry

For subtraction start with CLR C and use SUBB on both low and high bytes.
A plain SUB instruction does not exist.

STACK
Reset sets SP=07; a PUSH first increments SP, then writes. CALL pushes the
return address low byte first, then high; RET reverses that sequence. A
bare-metal MOV SP,#0x5F makes the first pushed byte land at 60, leaving 32
bytes through 7F. Reserve that area and check worst-case calls plus
interrupt nesting. The stack does not automatically grow into external
RAM. PUSH/POP accept direct byte addresses, not immediate data or an Rn
operand. PUSH 0x00 saves bank-0 R0, not necessarily the current bank's R0.

PORT READS
MOV A,P1 reads pins. Read-modify-write instructions with a port
destination (ANL P1,#mask, ORL P1,#mask, CPL P1.0 and friends) use the
output latch. That matters when external circuitry pulls a released input
low. Use masked or bit writes so unrelated outputs survive.

CODE51.TXT:
+------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                    04 / Practical assembly patterns                    |
+------------------------------------------------------------------------+

BIT TESTS AND COUNTED LOOPS
    mov r7,#10
again:
    ; body executes ten times
    djnz r7,again
    ret

Starting R7 at zero executes 256 iterations, not zero. DJNZ changes no
arithmetic flags. Conditional branches and SJMP have a signed -128..+127
byte displacement measured from the instruction AFTER the branch. For a
far condition, invert the test and use LJMP. AJMP/ACALL require the target
to share the 2-KiB page of the NEXT instruction, so code near a page
boundary needs special care.

UNSIGNED COMPARE
    cjne a,#10,different
    ; A == 10; CY is now 0
    sjmp done
different:
    jc below         ; unsigned A < 10
    ; otherwise A > 10
below:
done:
    ret

PACKED BCD
    mov a,#0x45
    add a,#0x38
    da a             ; A = 83 (hex encoding of decimal 83)
    ret

DA is for the result of packed-BCD ADD/ADDC with valid BCD operands. It is
not binary-to-decimal conversion and is not the correction for
subtraction. DA may set CY; it does not clear an existing carry. AC/OV are
not a decimal result test.

LOOKUP TABLE (DOS/51 PROGRAM)
    mov dptr,#table
    mov a,#2
    movc a,@a+dptr    ; A = ASCII '2'
    ret
table:
    db 48,49,50,51

CODE and XDATA overlap physically only where a BOARD wires them that way.
DOS/51's upper RAM is deliberately visible in both spaces, allowing its
assembler to write instructions with MOVX and then execute them. A generic
80C31 does not create executable RAM by itself.

MULTIPLY / DIVIDE
    mov a,#200
    mov 0xF0,#3      ; B
    mul ab           ; B:A = 0x0258 (600), CY=0, OV=1
    mov a,#200
    mov 0xF0,#7
    div ab           ; A=28 quotient, B=4 remainder, CY=0
    ret

DIV by zero sets OV and leaves A/B results undefined. Check B before
dividing. MUL and DIV are unsigned; signed multiplication/division need
additional sign handling.

ROTATE / SHIFT
RL/RR rotate within A and leave CY alone. RLC/RRC rotate the nine-bit CY:A
chain. For an unsigned right shift use CLR C followed by RRC A. A
multi-byte right shift starts at the high byte; a left shift starts at the
low byte. SWAP A exchanges nibbles; XCH exchanges whole bytes; XCHD
exchanges only the low nibbles of A and an indirectly addressed RAM byte.

MASKS
    anl 0x90,#0xFE   ; clear P1.0, preserve other latches
    orl 0x90,#0x01   ; set P1.0, preserve other latches
    cpl 0x90         ; BIT address 90: toggle P1.0

These examples use numeric SFR/bit addresses for DOS/51 portability. In a
desktop assembler, prefer named EQU/bit declarations from the exact chip
header. Do not assume another assembler's names, macros or directives
exist in the small on-board assembler.

SUBROUTINE CONTRACTS
Document inputs, outputs, scratch registers and flags. Save only what your
calling convention requires, but do not silently change the register bank.
RET restores PC, not A, B, PSW or DPTR. Interrupt entry likewise does not
preserve your working registers. For a callable DOS/51 program, keep the
shell's stack valid and restore any state you borrow. An endless loop,
disabled interrupts or a changed UART can make the shell appear dead;
Reset recovers execution but does not undo files overwritten on the RAM
disk.

DOS51.TXT:
+------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                  08 / DOS/51 lab and troubleshooting                   |
+------------------------------------------------------------------------+

WHAT THE EMULATOR ACTUALLY MODELS
Classic 80C31 CPU, 128-byte internal RAM, Timer 0/1, baseline interrupt
controller, UART and power-control states. The board adds an external
32-KiB ROM and two 32-KiB SRAMs, then implements SD-card SPI in software.
Timer 2, dual DPTR, enhanced address-recognition UART, IPH and analog
electrical behavior are not modeled. Reading the Philips extensions
chapter is not proof that those features run in this emulator.

BOARD MAP
CODE  0000-7FFF : DOS/51 ROM
CODE  8000-FFFF : upper SRAM (executable)
XDATA 0000-7FFF : lower SRAM (data)
XDATA 8000-FFFF : same upper SRAM as CODE
The RAM disk uses XDATA 2000-7FFF (24 KiB). Application/assembler/editor
storage uses the upper SRAM. Firmware state also occupies
internal/external RAM: those bytes are not all free application scratch
space.

SD CARD / FIELD MANUAL
A first-use browser card includes this ASCII field manual and DropBlocks.
Existing browser cards are not replaced. Use the Install field manual
button to add missing manual files to a FAT16 card; existing files with
the same names are left unchanged. FAT32 cards can be inserted for
firmware access, but the browser-side installer is FAT16-only.

    sdls
    sdget guide51.txt
    cat guide51.txt
    rm guide51.txt
    sdget mem51.txt
    cat mem51.txt

Remove an imported chapter from the RAM disk when done; the SD copy
remains. The full manual is split into small files because the RAM disk is
only 24 KiB and may already contain your work. If sdget reports
insufficient space, save/delete unneeded RAM files first; do not blank the
card to solve a RAM-disk capacity problem. Use the online edition for
search and the complete opcode table. Download card saves the actual FAT16
image with the text files in its root.

BOARD GPIO
P1.0-P1.3 are the example LED lines (active low). P1.4=/CS, P1.5=SCK,
P1.6=MOSI, P1.7=MISO for software SPI. Leave the MISO latch high for
input. Use bit instructions on LED bits; do not replace all of P1 with an
arbitrary byte while the SD card is attached. P0/P2 serve the external
memory bus; P3.0/1 serve the serial console; P3.6/7 serve external RAM
strobes.

The SPI protocol and FAT filesystem are firmware/board features, not CPU
instructions or on-chip 80C31 peripherals. A real SD card needs a 3.3-V
supply and suitable logic translation. The browser models digital
transactions, not regulator current, wire capacitance, analogue signal
edges or component damage.

GETTING UNSTUCK
- No console after a test: did you change Timer 1, SCON, PCON, SP or IE?
Reset restarts the ROM while preserving SRAM. Power cycle clears RAM and
RAM-disk files; the SD card has separate persistence.
- A conditional branch behaves strangely: check A rather than an imaginary
zero flag; check signed versus unsigned comparisons and whether an
instruction changed CY.
- Wrong RAM byte: distinguish #literal from direct address and MOV from
MOVX/MOVC. Check the selected register bank.
- A bit write hits the wrong peripheral: byte and bit addresses are
different namespaces. Only selected SFR bytes are bit-addressable.
- Table lookup reads nonsense: initialize A; MOVC adds it to DPTR or
post-opcode PC. It does not increment DPTR afterwards.
- RET jumps into nowhere: inspect unmatched PUSH/POP, stack overflow above
7F, corrupted return addresses or an unintended jump into a subroutine.
- A port will not go high: an output latch zero drives low; release it
with one for input. P0 GPIO needs pull-ups. On the actual ROMless board
many pins are already the memory bus.
- Timer counts at the wrong rate: classic timer mode is oscillator/12;
UART Timer 2 baud mode is a distinct Philips extension. A cycle table is
not an oscillator-clock table.
- New SD files are missing: an old saved card is intentionally preserved.
Click Install field manual; then sdls. Do not erase a visitor's saved work
just to seed a new example.

NEXT EXPERIMENTS
1. Change the printed character in first.asm and predict the ASCII code.
2. Add 0x7F+1 and 0xFF+1; inspect results and PSW with the debugger/memory
facilities available to your setup.
3. Build a lookup table and prove the difference between MOVC and MOVX.
4. Toggle only P1.0 while preserving all SD lines.
5. On a separate bare-metal ROM, build a Timer 0 ISR with an explicit
register-save contract; keep DOS/51's ROM untouched.

    sdget start51.txt
    cat start51.txt
    rm start51.txt

https://www.imania.dk/dos51/guide/

Philips 80C31/80C32 product specification, 7 August 2000;

READ ONE CHAPTER AT A TIME:
    sdget start51.txt
    cat start51.txt
    rm start51.txt

The last command removes the RAM-disk copy, NOT the SD original.
The RAM disk is 24 KiB. These files are deliberately split to fit.
Keep your own work; never blank the card just to install the guide.

WEB EDITION / SEARCH / OPCODE MAP:
https://www.imania.dk/dos51/guide/

Sources: Intel MCS-51 Family User's Manual (instruction set);
Philips 80C31/80C32 product specification, 7 August 2000;
DOS/51 firmware and emulator source in the ABN8051 repository.
Philips extensions are documented separately; the current emulator
implements the classic core. Physical stocked silicon is not bench-
verified for later-revision extensions. See PHIL51.TXT for scope.

INST1.TXT:
+------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                  03A / INSTRUCTION DESK: ACALL - LJMP                  |
+------------------------------------------------------------------------+

ACALL / FLOW
----------------------------------------
Push the address after this instruction and call a target in the same
2-KiB page as that return address. Uses two internal stack bytes; no
automatic register saves.

Example: acall worker
Watch: Use LCALL if placement is not guaranteed. Page bits are checked
against PC after the two-byte call.

OPERANDS                          BYTES MC  FLAGS
ACALL addr11                       2    2  -

ADD / ARITHMETIC
----------------------------------------
A = A + source; CY, AC and OV describe the unsigned, nibble and signed
results. Incoming CY is ignored.

Example: add a,#1
Watch: For multi-byte addition use ADD on the low byte and ADDC on
subsequent bytes.

OPERANDS                          BYTES MC  FLAGS
ADD A,#imm                         2    1  CY AC OV
ADD A,dir                          2    1  CY AC OV
ADD A,@Ri                          1    1  CY AC OV
ADD A,Rn                           1    1  CY AC OV

ADDC / ARITHMETIC
----------------------------------------
A = A + source + incoming CY. Updates CY, AC and OV.

Example: addc a,r2
Watch: Initialize carry deliberately if this is the first byte of a
calculation.

OPERANDS                          BYTES MC  FLAGS
ADDC A,#imm                        2    1  CY AC OV
ADDC A,dir                         2    1  CY AC OV
ADDC A,@Ri                         1    1  CY AC OV
ADDC A,Rn                          1    1  CY AC OV

AJMP / FLOW
----------------------------------------
Jump within the 2-KiB page containing the first byte after this
instruction. Does not push a return address.

Example: ajmp destination
Watch: Crossing a page boundary during layout can invalidate a previously
legal target.

OPERANDS                          BYTES MC  FLAGS
AJMP addr11                        2    2  -

ANL / LOGIC
----------------------------------------
Bitwise AND for byte operands. Boolean forms compute C AND bit or C AND
NOT bit; the / complements the source only.

Example: anl 0x90,#0xFE
Watch: Byte forms preserve CY/AC/OV unless explicitly writing PSW. Boolean
forms change C. Port destinations use their latch.

OPERANDS                          BYTES MC  FLAGS
ANL dir,A                          2    1  -
ANL dir,#imm                       3    2  -
ANL A,#imm                         2    1  -
ANL A,dir                          2    1  -
ANL A,@Ri                          1    1  -
ANL A,Rn                           1    1  -
ANL C,bit                          2    2  CY
ANL C,/bit                         2    2  CY

CJNE / FLOW
----------------------------------------
Compare without modifying either operand; branch if unequal. CY becomes 1
when the first operand is unsigned-less-than the second, otherwise 0.

Example: cjne a,#10,different
Watch: This is unsigned comparison, not a signed less-than instruction. CY
changes even if the branch is not taken.

OPERANDS                          BYTES MC  FLAGS
CJNE A,#imm,rel                    3    2  CY
CJNE A,dir,rel                     3    2  CY
CJNE @Ri,#imm,rel                  3    2  CY
CJNE Rn,#imm,rel                   3    2  CY

CLR / BITS
----------------------------------------
Clear A, C or one directly addressed bit. CLR A does not clear carry.

Example: clr c
Watch: Use CLR C before the first SUBB when no incoming borrow is
intended.

OPERANDS                          BYTES MC  FLAGS
CLR bit                            2    1  -
CLR C                              1    1  CY
CLR A                              1    1  -

CPL / BITS
----------------------------------------
Complement all bits in A, carry alone or a single directly addressed bit.

Example: cpl 0x90
Watch: CPL A leaves CY alone; CPL C toggles CY. A port-bit complement
reads the latch.

OPERANDS                          BYTES MC  FLAGS
CPL bit                            2    1  -
CPL C                              1    1  CY
CPL A                              1    1  -

DA / ARITHMETIC
----------------------------------------
Decimal-adjust A after packed-BCD ADD/ADDC, using the low nibble, AC, high
digit and CY. Can set carry for a decimal carry out; does not clear an
existing carry.

Example: da a
Watch: Only for valid packed-BCD addition. Not binary-to-BCD conversion or
decimal subtraction.

OPERANDS                          BYTES MC  FLAGS
DA A                               1    1  CY

DEC / ARITHMETIC
----------------------------------------
Subtract one modulo 256 from A, an Rn register, a direct byte or internal
RAM through @Ri. Does not update CY, AC or OV.

Example: dec r7
Watch: There is no DEC DPTR instruction. A becomes FF when decrementing
zero.

OPERANDS                          BYTES MC  FLAGS
DEC A                              1    1  -
DEC dir                            2    1  -
DEC @Ri                            1    1  -
DEC Rn                             1    1  -

DIV / ARITHMETIC
----------------------------------------
Unsigned divide A by B: quotient in A, remainder in B. CY is cleared; OV
is cleared for a nonzero divisor and set for zero.

Example: div ab
Watch: When B is zero A and B are undefined. Test the divisor first.

OPERANDS                          BYTES MC  FLAGS
DIV AB                             1    4  CY=0 OV

DJNZ / FLOW
----------------------------------------
Decrement an Rn register or direct byte modulo 256, then branch if that
result is nonzero. Arithmetic flags are unchanged.

Example: djnz r7,loop
Watch: An initial zero count wraps to FF and yields 256 iterations in a
bottom-tested loop.

OPERANDS                          BYTES MC  FLAGS
DJNZ dir,rel                       3    2  -
DJNZ Rn,rel                        2    2  -

INC / ARITHMETIC
----------------------------------------
Add one modulo 256 to a byte, or modulo 65536 to DPTR. Does not update CY,
AC or OV.

Example: inc dptr
Watch: DPTR is the only 16-bit INC destination; it does not provide a
carry flag on rollover.

OPERANDS                          BYTES MC  FLAGS
INC A                              1    1  -
INC dir                            2    1  -
INC @Ri                            1    1  -
INC Rn                             1    1  -
INC DPTR                           1    2  -

JB / FLOW
----------------------------------------
Branch when the addressed bit is one, leaving it unchanged.

Example: jb 0x90,high
Watch: A port test reads the pin; bit address 90 is P1.0, not the full P1
byte.

OPERANDS                          BYTES MC  FLAGS
JB bit,rel                         3    2  -

JBC / FLOW
----------------------------------------
If the addressed bit is one, clear it and branch. If zero, neither branch
nor clear has an effect.

Example: jbc 0x00,event
Watch: Useful for consuming a one-bit event flag. A port operation of this
kind uses the latch.

OPERANDS                          BYTES MC  FLAGS
JBC bit,rel                        3    2  -

JC / FLOW
----------------------------------------
Branch when CY is one.

Example: jc carry_out
Watch: After SUBB a set CY means borrow; after CJNE it means unsigned
less-than.

OPERANDS                          BYTES MC  FLAGS
JC rel                             2    2  -

JMP / FLOW
----------------------------------------
Set PC to DPTR plus unsigned A. This is the one hardware computed JMP
form.

Example: jmp @a+dptr
Watch: A generic JMP label accepted by some assemblers is a
pseudo-instruction, not an additional CPU opcode. A jump table must
contain executable jump entries or code at the computed address.

OPERANDS                          BYTES MC  FLAGS
JMP @A+DPTR                        1    2  -

JNB / FLOW
----------------------------------------
Branch when the addressed bit is zero without modifying it.

Example: jnb 0x99,wait_tx
Watch: TI is bit address 99; direct byte address 99 is the different SBUF
register.

OPERANDS                          BYTES MC  FLAGS
JNB bit,rel                        3    2  -

JNC / FLOW
----------------------------------------
Branch when CY is zero.

Example: jnc no_borrow
Watch: No-borrow is unsigned greater-or-equal after a properly initialized
SUBB.

OPERANDS                          BYTES MC  FLAGS
JNC rel                            2    2  -

JNZ / FLOW
----------------------------------------
Branch when A is not zero; no separate zero flag is consulted.

Example: jnz nonzero
Watch: An INC R7 followed by JNZ still tests A, not R7.

OPERANDS                          BYTES MC  FLAGS
JNZ rel                            2    2  -

JZ / FLOW
----------------------------------------
Branch when A is zero.

Example: jz empty
Watch: The branch neither clears A nor modifies carry.

OPERANDS                          BYTES MC  FLAGS
JZ rel                             2    2  -

LCALL / FLOW
----------------------------------------
Push the return PC and call any address in the 64-KiB CODE space.

Example: lcall worker
Watch: The stack is internal RAM. Budget two return-address bytes plus
software saves and nesting.

OPERANDS                          BYTES MC  FLAGS
LCALL addr16                       3    2  -

LJMP / FLOW
----------------------------------------
Replace PC with a full 16-bit CODE address.

Example: ljmp destination
Watch: No bank switching or external memory decoding is created by the
instruction.

OPERANDS                          BYTES MC  FLAGS
LJMP addr16                        3    2  -
